Salesforce (CRM) stock has lost 3.8% over the past twelve months, trailing the 17.3% return of the S&P 500. Executives say their job with artificial intelligence is to deliver new value to customers. During the fiscal Q2 2027 earnings call on August 26, 2026, management described an upgrade that most of its users have not made yet.

Salesforce Wants Its Customers On Premium Editions

Salesforce is waiting to sell its customers an upgrade. The company packages its newest AI features within premium editions of its software, and management noted that clients seeking these features must move to higher-end tiers. One such feature combines an AI model with the data a customer already stores inside Salesforce.

Few users have made the transition so far. Only 5% of the people who use Salesforce's sales and service software have upgraded to the higher-end editions, according to management. Yet the company stated that customers that have started using Salesforce's AI agents already spend about twice as much a year with the company, on average.

Agentforce's Recurring Revenue Is Small Beside The Whole Company

Agentforce, the company's product for AI agents, reached $1.5 billion of annual recurring revenue in fiscal Q2 2027. That figure remains a small fraction of the $43.9 billion of revenue Salesforce generated over the last twelve months.

The growth opportunity lies in the software those upgrades are sold into. Sales and service applications represent its two largest segments, posting $9.0 billion and $9.8 billion of revenue in fiscal 2026. Together they made up roughly 45% of the company's revenue that year, and each grew by about 8%.

Management has outlined broader ambitions for the business. In September, executives set a target of more than $63 billion in revenue for fiscal 2030. That compares with the $41.5 billion reported for fiscal 2026.

The share price appears to assume some of this growth already. The stock has risen 40% in the past three months, compared with 3.8% for the index. Still, the shares remain 11.5% below their 52-week high.

What Has Salesforce Not Yet Shown Investors?

Salesforce has not yet disclosed how much of Agentforce's revenue comes from customers who are past the trial stage. When asked about this during the August 26 call, management provided a count instead: the company added 2,000 paying customers into production, and said the number of accounts with agents in production grew 70% from the quarter before.

Users can now access Salesforce through tools like Slack without opening the company's dedicated software screens. Management said it is still determining how to charge for that access.

title: What Is Adobe No Longer Telling You?

What Is Adobe No Longer Telling You?

Image from Pexels

Adobe (ADBE) stock is priced at 12.9 times earnings, compared to a 21.9 multiple for the S&P 500. Yet even at that valuation, investors need to understand exactly what they hold as corporate priorities shift. Just a year ago, executives highlighted how much of the company's subscription revenue was influenced by AI. They no longer emphasize that measure. So what does Adobe point to now?

Adobe Now Points To A Narrower AI Number

The software maker now spotlights revenue specifically from products sold as AI products, which it brands as AI-first. On the fiscal Q4 2025 call, executives said that total new AI-influenced recurring revenue exceeded one-third of the business, after widening the measure to include the newer AI-first products.

This metric offers a much tighter lens than the previous standard. During the fiscal Q3 2025 call, leadership stated that recurring revenue influenced by AI had passed $5 billion. By the following quarter, executives said their strategy was to drive all recurring revenue through AI-influenced products. That broader measure served to signal that AI was already a component of what many customers were paying for.

Adobe's AI Products Are Still A Small Business

This AI-first recurring revenue accounted for more than 2% of Adobe's $27.5 billion in total recurring revenue during fiscal Q3 2026. The former metric painted a vastly larger picture. On the fiscal Q4 2025 call, executives noted the AI-influenced figure exceeded one-third of all recurring revenue, adding that the newer AI-first products were factored into that total.

Even so, these dedicated AI products are expanding at a much sharper clip than the broader business. Executives reported that AI-first recurring revenue grew more than 150% from a year earlier, while total recurring revenue increased 11.2%. For context, during the fiscal Q1 2025 call, leadership said the AI-first lineup had contributed more than $125 million of recurring revenue.

Customer engagement with the tools is also rising. According to executives, AI usage picked up from the prior quarter across both Creative Cloud and the Firefly app.

Should Adobe Shareholders Welcome The Narrower Number?

Yes, with two caveats. The narrower metric counts only AI products that customers actually pay for, and it is growing quickly, so it is the stricter of the two measures. That provides a reassuring signal for those holding the stock.

The risk lies in the scale of those products. They remain a small fraction of the overall business, meaning the bulk of an investment in Adobe is tied to the rest of the subscription base. At the same time, the company is giving more away to acquire users. Monthly users of its free creative products passed 100 million, up more than 70% from a year earlier. Contracted future revenue grew 8% over the same period. When asked in September about posting the first single-digit growth in that metric since early fiscal 2023, executives tied the pace to their focus on signing up free users, noting the figure steps up in the fourth quarter.

This slide has occurred during a month when the enterprise software group that includes SoundHound moved higher. Across that same past-month window, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 2%, suggesting that the broader equities market has held steady.

Meanwhile, shares of Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) are at $239.03, down 3% over the past month, representing a far smaller decline than the drop in SoundHound stock. Shares of ServiceNow (NYSE:NOW) trade at $139.11, up 5% over the past month, moving in the opposite direction from SoundHound stock.

Software Rally Leaves SoundHound Behind

Put together, the figures point to a decline specific to SoundHound stock. Large enterprise vendors selling AI agents, along with the broader software fund, held up or climbed over the same month in which SoundHound shares fell sharply. That pattern rules out the explanation many readers might reach for first: a broad markdown of companies building AI agents.

The bull market has continued its impressive run, but Bank of America is warning investors that the road ahead could become considerably more difficult. While corporate earnings remain strong and AI spending continues to support growth, the bank sees mounting risks that could make it harder for stocks to maintain their upward momentum. And with expectations already running high, even strong earnings results might not be enough to keep investors happy.

Heading into the third-quarter earnings season, Bank of America expects earnings per share to grow by 32%, with tech and power companies benefiting from continued AI investment and rising energy demand. However, the bank is less optimistic about the broader market, anticipating slower year-over-year earnings growth outside those sectors. More concerning is its outlook for 2027, when higher interest rates, commodity pressures, geopolitical tensions, and uncertainty surrounding AI spending could present additional challenges.

Bank of America strategist Savita Subramanian explains why investors shouldn't take the market's recent strength for granted: "Following big positive surprises in the last two quarters, healthy beats are the status quo and may not be enough to drive stocks higher. Investors will likely be listening for reassurance that growth can be sustained despite rates and commodity pressure. 2027 risks are skewed to the downside in our view. Ultimately, index EPS remains highly dependent on the durability of the AI capex cycle and successful monetization, but the interplay between geopolitics, rates and Tech may be underestimated – a higher cost of capital and geopolitical bottlenecks could gum up what has so far been a mostly smooth story."

title: Salesforce’s biggest risk now is customers who never log in
detail:
Salesforce’s biggest risk now is customers who never log in
Opeyemi Babalola
Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:34 AM MDT 5 min read
CRM
ANTH.PVT
Trade CRM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

For many salespeople, the workday starts with a chore. They open Salesforce, click through accounts and update deal fields before the first call.

At Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, that chore had already moved somewhere else. Its sales teams were working in Salesforce through Claude rather than Salesforce's own interface, Patrick Stokes, Salesforce's president of applications and marketing, told CIO.com in August.

That habit sits at the center of the biggest debate around Salesforce Inc. (CRM), whose software helps companies track customers, deals and service requests. Its stock has become a referendum on whether AI agents help or hurt business software.

Salesforce insists the shift works in its favor, with Stokes arguing that agentic use "dramatically increases the value of Salesforce." Investors spent most of 2026 betting the other way.

In February, a Jefferies trader coined the term "SaaSpocalypse" as fear of AI agents sent software stocks tumbling. Salesforce did not escape the rout.

Also read: BofA splits software into winners and losers as AI agents arrive

Bank of America analyst Tal Liani took up that fear directly in his report, "Upgrading to Buy: a sound strategy that addresses the AI risks and opportunities." According to the BofA note shared with TheStreet, the firm raised Salesforce to Buy from Underperform and lifted its price target to $285 from $160.

Even so, the stock remains about 15% below its 52-week high, according to the BofA note.

Salesforce is betting the screen matters less

According to the note, Bank of America's earlier caution centered on disintermediation, the risk that AI cuts Salesforce out of its own customer relationships.

The note frames the shift neatly: "AI 3.0 is the interface." In plain English, a worker may type a request into Claude or Slack and never open the underlying app at all.

That sounds like bad news for a company whose brand lives on a login page. However, BofA argues the screen was never where most of the value sat. The rules on who can see a record and what an agent may change still live inside Salesforce.

Think of it as a building's front door versus its wiring. Tenants can use a new entrance, but the lights still run on the old circuits. According to the BofA note, reaching Salesforce data "is not equivalent to replacing the applications" that govern it.

Bank of America raised Salesforce to Buy from Underperform and lifted its price target to $285 from $160, citing lower AI disintermediation risk.wdstock / Getty Images
Salesforce is charging more, not less, for AI access

Instead of discounting as the screen loses importance, Salesforce is raising the price of access. Its new top tier, which bundles Claudeforce, costs 39% more than the Advanced edition, according to the BofA note. That is a bold bet that customers will pay extra to use Salesforce inside someone else's chatbot.
